claims.text: The initial cast, homogenized CoCrFeNiMn-based high-entropy alloy has a relatively coarse-grained, near-single-phase microstructure.
The proposed treatment consists of hot rolling at about 950°C, rapid quenching, and aging at 500–600°C for 1–4 hours.
High-temperature hot rolling will produce significant plastic deformation and grain refinement.
Rapid quenching will retain the hot-deformed structure.
Aging at 500–600°C will precipitate ultrafine, coherent secondary phases.
The combined treatment will generate a dual-phase microstructure containing refined grains and uniformly dispersed ultrafine coherent precipitates.
Nanoscale coherent precipitates hinder dislocation motion and provide precipitation strengthening.
The refined grain structure preserves ductile deformation while precipitation strengthening raises strength.
The heterogeneous dual-phase microstructure activates energy-dissipative mechanisms that improve ductility and fracture resistance.
The treatment will increase Young's modulus through the proposed microstructural changes.
Relative to a rapidly quenched single-phase baseline, the treatment will improve yield strength.
Relative to the baseline, the treatment will increase Young's modulus.
Relative to the baseline, the treatment will improve fracture resistance.
Relative to the baseline, the treatment will maintain or improve ductility.
Conventionally processed high-entropy alloys typically exhibit a trade-off between strength and ductility.
Over-aging can cause precipitate coarsening and embrittlement.
The beneficial effect requires sufficient hot deformation to produce a fine grain structure.
The hypothesis may fail in alloy compositions that do not support coherent precipitate formation.
The magnitudes of property improvements depend on alloy composition and processing parameters.

Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in all four targeted properties, or failure to observe the proposed refined and precipitate-containing microstructure, would falsify the hypothesis.
